subject: Daylight saving time
hook: DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Daylight saving time was not invented to help farmers, but was actually first implemented as a wartime measure to conserve coal.
angle_support: The first nation-wide implementations were by the German and Austro-Hungarian Empires, both starting on 30 April 1916.

The first states to adopt DST (German: Sommerzeit) nationally were those of the German Empire and its World War I ally Austria-Hungary commencing on 30 April 1916, as a way to conserve coal during wartime.
title: The Real Reason Daylight Saving Time Was Invented
description: Many people believe daylight saving time was created for farmers, but the historical record shows it was actually first adopted by nations during World War I to save coal. This video explores the true origins of the clock shift.
narration: DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture farmers needing extra hours in the fields. It was actually closer to a strategic wartime necessity. The concept was never about helping the agricultural industry thrive. The first national implementation occurred in April 1916. The German and Austro-Hungarian Empires mandated the change as a desperate measure to conserve coal supplies during World War I. Britain and the United States followed shortly after. It started not for the harvest, but for the war.
